note.question: Can firms profit from giving consumers informed control over data collection, and when does strategic privacy consent help or hurt consumers under behavior-based pricing?
note.overview: Two horizontally differentiated firms strategically choose opt-in rewards and intertemporal prices while forward-looking consumers choose firms and privacy consent. The article solves the resulting two-period behavior-based-pricing game and compares consent regimes.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In period 1, firms choose opt-in rewards and first-period prices; consumers choose a firm, purchase, and opt in or out. In period 2, firms choose behavior-based prices for identifiable old customers and unidentifiable new customers, after which consumers repurchase or switch. Privacy consent determines whether the incumbent can recognize and price discriminate against a returning consumer. Opt-in rewards endogenize consumer data provision and can soften first-period price competition.
